limitations: Original source selectors distinguish Snowsant S1 BOTH/farthest INPUT, S2 farthest-ground trigger then target-centered radius0.7 CAST with no victim cap (limitTargetNum0). Native selector-source centering is mapped to the farthest trigger victim; C# centering dispatch remains unverified, Almond S1 ground/normal INPUT and S2 BOTH/farthest INPUT. Numerical abnormal-combination masks are retained, but the native C# enum loader has not been recovered; engine targetability remains bounded.

Original begin hit events, declared clip alias speeds, maxAnimScale, ranged projectile speeds, charged SP ranks, source end clips and minimum postdelay are used. Continuous pulling follows the existing weight/force-aware simulator pull primitive, not reconstructed native trajectory physics.

Snowsant S2 native firstPartTime0.3/secondPartTime1 and random lateral offset remain uninterpreted trajectory fields. The adapter bounds its link to1.3s after impact without inventing a C# trajectory or native random draw order.

Almond S2 original hit_interval1.5 and hit_duration4 bind-and-hit sequence is timed from accepted hook impact. Native C# link-versus-skill clock phase is unverified; end clips and early target-loss finish are explicit bounded interpretations.

Snowsant infection-tag talent force increment and silence use source blackboards; ON_BUFF_FINISH target/source dispatcher phase is bounded to cast completion. Sluggish source durationKey-stun binding is preserved; selected sluggish blackboard follows original skill table.

Almond talent source ON_SKILL_FINISH forced SP applies once per battle at full hook completion. Redeployment does not rearm the first-activation grant. Native cancel-before-release talent dispatch remains unverified.

All models retain source facing hashes and original clips. Unity hook/net lines, original particle effects, modules, actual-game frame comparisons and the native dynamic-attack classification enum are not enabled or claimed.
